_note: Deductions an employee in India can have. Seeded once; edit them on the Deduction types page.

types.name: Provident fund (EPF)
types.description: 12% of PF wages (basic + DA, at least 50% of pay under the Labour Codes), capped at the wage ceiling unless PF is on full wages.

types.name: ESI
types.description: 0.75% of gross for employees earning up to the ESI wage limit, in notified areas.

types.name: Professional tax
types.description: State slab tax on monthly salary (Telangana: up to Rs 200 a month).

types.name: Labour welfare fund
types.description: State contribution, usually yearly or half-yearly, per the state's LWF rule.

types.name: Income tax (TDS)
types.description: Tax on salary for the year under the chosen regime, spread over the remaining months.

types.name: Voluntary provident fund (VPF)
types.description: Extra PF over the statutory 12%, up to 100% of basic + DA. Old regime: counts toward 80C.

types.name: NPS (employee contribution)
types.description: Employee's own NPS contribution through payroll. Old regime: 80CCD(1) within 80C, extra 80CCD(1B).

types.name: Group health insurance (employee share)
types.description: Employee's share of the company health or family floater premium.

types.name: Donation (PM CARES / charity)
types.description: Donation made through payroll. Old regime: 80G, with the employer's certificate.

types.name: Salary advance recovery
types.description: Monthly recovery of an advance; set the last month so it stops when repaid.

types.name: Employee loan EMI
types.description: Interest-free or concessional loans above Rs 20,000 can be a taxable perquisite.
